title: Scraper: Extend ASUS to Threadripper / Threadripper Pro
description:

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Extend the existing AsusScraper to cover Threadripper (sTRX4/sTR5) and Threadripper Pro (sWRX8/sWRX9) ASUS consumer + workstation boards.

board_class: Threadripper, ThreadripperPro.

ASUS boards in scope:
- sTRX4: ROG Zenith II Extreme, Prime TRX40-Pro
- sTR5: ROG Zenith TRX50, Prime TRX50-Sage WiFi
- sWRX8: Pro WS WRX80E-Sage SE WiFi
- sWRX9: Pro WS WRX90E-Sage SE

Implementation:
- src/psp_etl/scrape/asus.py uses SOCKET_SUBSPECS = {'AM4': 532, 'AM5': 172178} for the odinapi.asus.com SeriesFilterResult call. Need to discover the corresponding SubSpec IDs for sTRX4, sTR5, sWRX8, sWRX9.
- Method: load https://www.asus.com/motherboards-components/motherboards/all-series/?Series=ProductLevel2Code in a browser, switch the socket filter, watch the XHR for the SubSpec param.
- AM5_CHIPSETS / AM4_CHIPSETS regexes need a TR/TR-Pro counterpart for socket detection from board model name (TRX40, TRX50, WRX80, WRX90 tokens).
- Add a SOCKET regex match path or a fall-through on the chipset regex.

Coordination with #85 (ASUS Server): Pro WS WRX80E/WRX90E sit awkwardly between consumer and server lines; ASUS classifies them as workstation. Decide which scraper picks them up — recommend this consumer scraper, since the support download flow is identical to consumer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Existing AM4/AM5 tests pass
- New tests for at least one TRX40 and one WRX80E board parse and ZIP unwrap
- SubSpec IDs documented in code comments

Related: #79, #81.
